content.text:
Validation: The followup reproduced equal acceptance: both arms passed fixed model checking, simulation and behavior in **2 attempts**.

| Pair | Raw final / tool seconds | Structured final / tool seconds |
|---|---|---|
| Original | `run-fef27c31a32143f6923faa8836a69dca` / 12.208444291 | `run-180f007d16724c469a19e5514f6c9662` / 10.258247792 |
| Followup | `run-948d4dce9e87423ca6a5d7a4d96b5d9a` / 9.750073082 | `run-b1f3eddf85364fcd8e67902f9d133d74` / 11.672195292 |

Detailed evidence **was available on direct inspection**, superseding the executor’s availability report. Followup baselines passed model checking but failed simulation initialization; baseline behavior was not evaluated. Correction logs showed checking and simulation success; behavior acceptance comes only from the fixed finals above.

Structured baseline feedback retained 5/29 lines, omitting 24. Correction `run-cbcbed9f139640fe8d94f10715029670` omitted all 25 lines, producing empty diagnostics despite success messages in the raw log. These counts are now verified; empty diagnostics alone do not establish acceptance.

The two pairs show no observed pass-rate or attempt-count advantage. The tool-time ordering reversed between pairs. With only two pairs on one task, no general Harness benefit or causal speed improvement is established. Tokens, costs and total model/workflow timing are missing; seed and temperature controls are unavailable. Latest native usage was **66/100 requests**, superseding 61/100.

A future study could use more tasks and repetitions with explicit success feedback and complete timing/token measurements. **Stopped at validated, with all 12 runs consumed; no further experiments or analysis record created.**
